title: Adversarial Robustness via Deformable Convolution with Stochasticity
summary: Core gradient-similarity sufficiency bound fails for valid shared random convolution; empirical robustness remains untested.

problems.claim: n<=S^2 epsilon_c guarantees expected gradient cosine <=epsilon_c
problems.location: PDF p4 Lemma1 Eq8; p5 Eq12; p13 Eqs20-21
assumptions: Nonzero cross-entropy input gradients at zero input
problems.check: Exact 25 masks,625 ordered pairs; each gradient support2500; intersection expectation ((13*50-10)/(25*50))^2=4096/15625=.262144>.25.
problems.result: Sufficiency claim false for shared masks; necessary-only interpretation distinguished.
problems.counterevidence: Spatially independent masks would be a different operator; default code uses other n; neither removes universal shared-convolution counterexample. Empirical scores not reproduced.
problems.impact: Invalid data-independent core guarantee; experiment failure not claimed.
problems.correction: No general repair certified; merely weakening intermediate sufficient bound is invalid.

independent_verification.original_claim_and_location: Read physical pp3-5 Definition1, Lemma1 Eq8, the stated small-similarity guarantee and Eq12; read and visually checked AppendixA.1 p13 Eqs18-21. Read the named static shared-mask and BPDA code regions.
independent_verification.operative_assumptions: Kernel5x5, stride2, one uniformly selected offset per forward pass, independently resampled across passes and spatially shared as in the released convolution. Valid103x103 input yields50x50 outputs and2500 nonzero input-gradient entries. A summed-logit cross-entropy readout at zero input gives a common nonzero gradient scalar, which cancels from cosine; convolution weights are unrestricted by the lemma.
independent_verification.decisive_check: Fresh coordinate-set calculation used five one-dimensional supports {a,a+2,...,a+98}. The sum of their25 pairwise intersection sizes is640=13*50-10. Independence of coordinate offsets gives E cosine=(640/1250)^2=4096/15625=.262144, above epsilon=.25 while n=1<=4epsilon. No ratio-of-expectations or MonteCarlo approximation is used because every gradient norm is constant.
independent_verification.alternatives_and_counterevidence: The published sufficient guarantee is explicit in p4 following Eq8 and p5 Eq12. A merely necessary interpretation of the lemma is not contradicted; a different operator with independent masks per output location is outside this construction. Even replacing <= by strict< would not rescue the guarantee: epsilon=.26 gives n=1<1.04 but .262144>.26. Released n=3 defaults do not restrict the universal lemma to that setting.
independent_verification.core_dependency_and_severity: Major retained on the central data-independent upper-bound guarantee. Eq20 admits no n=1 at epsilon=.25 (bound=-11/16), whereas its relaxation admits it; the loss of sufficiency is confirmed by an actual valid convolution. No benchmark accuracy is inferred.
independent_verification.repair_scope: No universal repair is claimed. Eq20 cannot simply be certified without revisiting the preceding probability/gradient argument. Ancillary A.2 and attack-code concerns remain explicitly unadjudicated; static BPDA loop indeed averages completed deltas, not per-update gradients, but historical table provenance is not established.
